v3.comment: UI rework grammar (issue #54), Compose only. Deliberately its own top-level category: the Style Dictionary platforms filter on `color` / `font` / `spacing` / `component`, so nothing in here reaches Sources/FitUI/Tokens/Generated or android/src/main/res. The Compose mirror is android/src/main/kotlin/com/fit321/fitui/v3/tokens/FitV3Colors.kt; values come from the prototype (prototypes/flows/coach/dashboard-drafts.html, the .k-alpha block) and from the athlete .fit-light recipe, which is canonical over the spec table.

tinted.comment: The tinted canvas IS the screen, top to bottom — not a wash behind a header. Nothing below it carries its own colour.

tinted-glow.comment: Painted over the base gradient. Centre sits above the top edge, so the brightest point is off-screen and the screen opens on the fall-off.

light.comment: The athlete keeps the existing light canvas — the rework changes the shapes, not the background.

light-glow.comment: The same brand breath at roughly half the strength: on #F2F2F7 the dark alphas read as a stain.

tinted.comment: Panel, card, chip, input, segmented, stepper, select row. A flat darkening of the canvas — no blur, no opaque fill.

tinted-hairline.comment: Inset 1px edge. On tinted the edge comes from the hairline; on light it comes from the shadow.

light-shadow.comment: Reuses the existing card lift (FitElevation.fitCardElevation) rather than inventing a second shadow.

tinted.comment: Anything that sits ON a surface: avatar, icon plate, face.

face-tinted.comment: A face in a STACK is opaque — translucent faces show each other through. One fill per canvas hue; teal is the shipped one.

on-canvas-tinted.comment: Raised directly on the canvas (the identity avatar, a header circle) rather than on a surface — the canvas is darker than a panel, so the plate is a touch lighter.

on-canvas-light.comment: On #F2F2F7 a raised plate goes lighter than the canvas, not darker — gray.100 would read as a hole.

status.comment: Status colours split by look for the same reason the canon ones do: a red that reads on a dark canvas is too bright on white, and a yellow perimeter at the 400 step disappears on it.

badge-review-ink.comment: A review badge is yellow; white on yellow is the unreadable pair, so its number goes dark in both looks.

control.comment: A control ON a field surface — the stepper's round buttons. One step away from the field rather than the plate step, which on white is too faint to find.

avatar-ring.comment: The halo around the profile avatar. It exists to lift the avatar off the tinted canvas; on light there is nothing to lift it from, and the prototype has no light recipe for it, so it is deliberately absent rather than accidentally invisible.

tinted.comment: The one solid object on a coloured screen. Flat teal was tried and rejected 2026-09-14: the brand gradient is already the canvas, so a gradient button has nothing to stand out against.

tinted-highlight.comment: Inset hairline on the top edge — paper, not plastic.

light.comment: On the light canvas the brand gradient still reads, so primary stays as it is today.

tinted.comment: Sheets, menus, snackbars. Blur belongs here and nowhere else — a sheet is a layer above the screen, and the screen showing through is what says so.

snackbar.comment: The snackbar is dark in BOTH looks — it floats over content rather than replacing a surface, so it does not follow the canvas. On light it is the same near-black the canon snackbar has always been; on tinted it is the bar colour with a blur behind it.

chrome.comment: The screen's OWN header and footer. On the tinted canvas they are transparent and the gradient runs under them (`.fit-phone.fit-dark.k-alpha > .fit-phone-header/.fit-phone-footer`); `bar` below is for a bar that floats over scrolling content, which is a different job.

accent-badge.comment: The canon `.fit-badge-accent` — a value that is good news next to a number (the week's trend).

from.comment: The day ring's own gradient (`#cdgrad`) — it starts a step off the brand blue.

tinted.comment: Bars over scrolling content (header, footer) — translucent, so the canvas keeps running underneath.

selected-light-fill.comment: The brand wash at 10%, not a flat tint: `bg.brand-subtle` is teal-600 at 16%, which on a white row reads as a solid mint block rather than a selection.

segmented-selected-tinted.comment: Only the tinted look drops the selection gradient: teal on a teal canvas does not separate. On light the gradient stays, because a white tab on a white track is invisible.

dashed-tinted.comment: The add row's border. Stronger than the divider on purpose — it is the only affordance on an otherwise empty panel.

circle-outline-tinted.comment: An action circle that is not the expected answer: outline only.

action-primary-label-tinted.comment: The label under the filled circle. On the tinted canvas the fill is white, so the word cannot be — it goes plain white; on light the fill is the brand gradient and the word carries the brand colour.

strip-tinted.comment: The session card's location strip — a deeper inset of the same surface, not a second card.

pick-tick.comment: The tick inside a filled check circle — dark on teal in both looks.

geometry.comment: Measurements the rework adds. Values that already exist (radius 14/16, screen inset 16) are referenced, not redeclared.
